values.description:
Output of the `/game-concept` skill: **the full spec directory** `concept/spec/{slug}/` — `CONCEPT.md`, `00-CORE.md`, five numbered layer sheets, `research/`, `OPEN.md`, `HANDOFF.md`.

**Read `HANDOFF.md` first.** It is a subject index built for exactly this handoff. The routing rule is: read `CONCEPT.md`, `00-CORE.md`, and every numbered sheet up to and including the deepest layer your work touches.

**Provenance tags set your latitude.** `[you said]` / `[you chose]` are binding. `[you accepted]` is provisionally binding. `[I assumed]` is a starting point you may argue with. `OPEN.md §4` is the work queue; `§2` carries the batched defaults for audio, visual feedback, technical shape, measurement and live-ops.

**Leads read the source sheets directly. Do not paraphrase the brief down the hierarchy** — each retelling is a re-interpretation, and interpretation is where variance re-enters.

values.spawns: Fantasy Lead · Setting Lead · Tone Lead · Lore Lead · Identity Lead · Vocabulary Lead
values.description: Establishes the fiction the whole game is dressed in, then delegates each narrative layer to a domain lead.
values.does_not_own: Any gameplay rule, system, or mechanic — this category names and dresses things, it does not define how they function.

values.owns: the one-line fantasy · what the player becomes · the emotional promise · what makes it feel good to inhabit
values.description: Defines the core power fantasy the player is buying into and the promises the game makes about it.
values.does_not_own: How that fantasy is delivered mechanically
values.must_verify: **Search Roblox for games already selling this fantasy before committing to it.** The brief's research established that the noun cannot differentiate; the same is true of the fantasy. Cite what you found, including the near-misses.

values.description:
**What the build stage can actually produce today.** A machine-readable list of available patterns and parameters, mirroring `ui-forge`'s pattern registry and its `validateBrief` gate.

Every verification pass checks its category's specs against this. A spec naming a capability not listed does not silently fail three stages later: it fails here, and either the spec changes or the capability becomes an explicit build-stage request.

*Known current limits, as of wave 2:* `ui-forge` exports **two** patterns — `modal-grid` (a centred dismissible panel holding a grid of items) and `hud-overlay` (a persistent HUD). The real limit is narrower than "no HUD": `hud-overlay` marks nothing `PRESSABLE` by default, which is a default rather than a proven incapability. Read `ui-forge/src/compose/index.mjs` for the live list — `npm run capabilities` prints it. *An earlier version of this line said a persistent HUD was not buildable; it had not been true since `hud-overlay` landed, and two wave-2 agents flagged it independently.*
